solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: 'intact' is the direct opposite of the clue and 'duplicate'/'living' are implausible; the colon clause (lacked skull and most of tail) gives the word away, so this is very easy
S032-01.notes: The skeleton was missing its skull and tail, so the specimen was fragmentary. 'Intact' contradicts the text, 'duplicate' clashes with 'single', and 'living' makes no sense for a skeleton.

S032-02.notes: Supporters went from wavering to quickly backing the bill, so the speech roused them to act: galvanized. Alienated and bewildered go the wrong way, and outnumbered does not fit. Students who don't know the word 'galvanized' can still eliminate the other three.

flags: minor: D is weak, since the final sentence supports the point rather than rejecting a comparison; B (photography) is never mentioned
S032-03.notes: The third sentence ('Although extremely long, only a few meters wide... similar color') explains why the wall is hard to see.

flags: minor: the facts check out (studies by Reimchen, and by Helfield & Naiman, on marine-derived 15N in riparian trees and faster Sitka spruce growth). 'Leaves' is loose wording for conifers such as spruce, whose leaves are needles, but it is acceptable
S032-04.notes: Bears carry salmon inland, and nearby trees show ocean-type nitrogen and faster growth, which points to salmon bringing ocean nutrients to the forest. A (direct uptake of seawater) is unsupported, C (bears grow faster) is never discussed, and D reverses cause and effect.

S032-05.notes: The gap is 45-38=7 points for ages 18-29 versus 55-14=41 points for 65 and older, and only D gives both numbers for both groups. A (virtual tours only) and B (in-person only) are traps that cover one column. C covers the wrong age group.

flags: minor: A closely restates Text 2's last sentence ('inviting the listener to signal'), which makes it easy to find
S032-06.notes: The linguists in Text 2 find the rise on statements speakers are sure of and say it works as a check on the listener, not a sign of doubt. B wrongly concedes doubt. C and D are not supported.

S032-07.notes: The goal is to stress the length of the wait, and only C gives the 17-hour maximum. A stresses the short 15-minute delay instead. The facts match Kabadayi & Osvath 2017 (Science).

S032-08.notes: The second sentence qualifies the first (no tailpipe emissions, but battery manufacturing emits), so a contrast is needed: Even so. The other three transitions signal cause, similarity or restatement.

S032-09.notes: The opening modifier 'Excavated...' must describe the body. A and D make it modify the peat cutters or the people (dangling modifier), and D also repeats 'the people who found it'. C's 'there was' leaves the modifier dangling and the comma clause is awkward. The facts are accurate: Tollund Man, found in 1950 and mistaken for a recent murder victim.

S032-10.notes: Two independent clauses are joined by the conjunctive adverb 'however', which needs a semicolon before it and a comma after. A and B are comma splices. C leaves out the comma after 'however', which is the subtle trap.
